correctness.rationale: For one uniform m-point coordinate, translate an oscillation<=1 vector into [0,1]^m. The log centered exponential functional has strictly positive second derivative with respect to each coordinate at fixed others: λ²w(1−w)>0. Thus every maximum is a 0/1 cut, nonconstant by Jensen, giving sharp factor H_m(k). Conditional exponential integration over successive coordinates yields product upper bound with equality attained by sums of cuts. The equality argument is substantive: the conditional mean h on earlier coordinates itself maximizes; across a cut edge h varies by exactly one, so every fiber of f must have the same full signed difference. The product of complete bipartite cut graphs is connected, so the residual last-coordinate function is independent of earlier coordinates and separately a binary cut. The neighboring H_m ratio gives threshold B_m(λ), with derivative negative because sinh(mt)>m sinh(t); endpoints (m−1)/2 and zero count all tie values. The smooth gλ(p) has unique interior max pλ and second derivative −λ², giving the lattice squared-distance discrepancy with Oλ(m^−3) remainder; fractional parts of irrational pλ are dense, including p_1=1−1/(e−1). The source's integer bounded-difference polytope test and small-alphabet finite checks are supplementary, not infinite proofs. A numerical independent check of the lattice error and staircase is consistent; strict convexity/tensor equality bears universal conclusion.
residual_risks: Finite numerical or exhaustive small-parameter checks do not prove unbounded cases; only the reconstructed analytic argument supports universal claims.
